n0001.title: The Scaling Hypothesis
n0001.gist: GPT-3's surprising leap from mere scale reveals that simply making neural networks bigger unlocks meta-learning and generality, vindicating the once-fringe scaling hypothesis as a path toward AGI.

n0002.title: Introducing GPT-3's Meta-Learning
n0002.gist: GPT-3's huge scale-up produced not just more knowledge but genuine meta-learning, reviving the scaling hypothesis as a serious theory of intelligence.

n0003.title: GPT-3 And The Scaling Hypothesis
n0003.gist: GPT-3's unexpected success at massive scale shows neural networks becoming more general and Bayesian as they grow, confirming the scaling hypothesis.

n0006.title: Meta-Learning
n0006.gist: GPT-3 learns new tasks purely from prompted examples, showing genuine learned meta-learning rather than memorized text patterns.

n0009.title: GPT-3's Emergent Abilities
n0009.gist: Despite its crude, outdated architecture, GPT-3 displays startling creative and reasoning abilities that standard benchmarks fail to capture, while unsupervised pretraining keeps scaling smoothly.

n0010.title: Flexing GPT
n0010.gist: GPT-3's flashy demonstrations of jokes, code, and meta-learning reveal capabilities far beyond what standard NLP benchmarks measure.

n0015.title: Baking The Cake
n0015.gist: GPT-3's continued smooth scaling despite its cost shows unsupervised pretraining is a real, still-rising layer of the AI cake, not a dead end.

n0023.title: Scaling And The Scaling Hypothesis
n0023.gist: GPT-3's loss keeps falling predictably with scale, and this blessing of scale, where bigger models generalize better rather than worse, supports the radical claim that scale alone drives intelligence.

n0024.title: Scaling
n0024.gist: GPT-3's performance follows the same clean power-law scaling curves predicted by theory, with much room left to improve.

n0033.title: Blessings Of Scale
n0033.gist: Across many domains, deep learning models get more stable, general, and human-like simply by growing bigger, not by adding cleverness.

n0039.title: Occam's Razor Explanation
n0039.gist: Large models act as ensembles of countless sub-models that, given enough data, favor genuinely generalizing algorithms over superficial shortcuts, explaining why scale induces meta-learning.

n0047.title: Scaling Hypothesis
n0047.gist: The strong scaling hypothesis holds that a single scalable architecture, trained ever larger, will spontaneously develop sophisticated intelligence, a claim once dismissed as numerology but now vindicated.

n0051.title: Why Does Pretraining Work?
n0051.gist: Pretraining forces a model to keep shrinking its prediction error, and the last, hardest-won bits of that error correspond to real understanding, though whether this fully explains GPT-3 remains debated.

n0052.title: The Pretraining Thesis
n0052.gist: Because human writing implicitly encodes causality and reasoning, a model that predicts text well enough must learn to understand the world, not just its surface statistics.

n0057.title: Stages Of Learning
n0057.gist: As training proceeds, a language model climbs from letter frequencies to spelling to word associations to syntax to semantics, each stage squeezing out more bits of error.

n0066.title: The Last Bits
n0066.gist: The final fractions of a bit of error separate ordinary text generation from human-level understanding, since only genuine reasoning captures the rare, long-tail cases humans handle effortlessly.

n0075.title: Reasons For Doubt
n0075.gist: The pretraining thesis is logically neat but unproven in practice, resembling past theoretical AI schemes needing infeasible resources, until GPT-3 showed the needed compute was actually affordable.

n0080.title: Open Questions
n0080.gist: Nobody predicted GPT-3's scaling gains in advance, and nobody yet knows what a further, similarly-sized scale-up would produce.

n0087.title: Prospects
n0087.gist: Whether an AI arms race follows GPT-3 depends less on available hardware than on which organizations have the conviction to actually commit to scaling.

n0088.title: Precedents For Scaling
n0088.gist: History suggests that once a hard problem is known to be solvable and the ingredients exist, someone will realize it quickly, as with the atomic bomb and, per its own architects, GPT-3.

n0092.title: Hardware Overhang
n0092.gist: Major labs already have the hardware and budgets to scale far beyond GPT-3, so the real bottleneck is a lack of institutional belief in the scaling hypothesis.

n0096.title: Google, DeepMind, And OpenAI
n0096.gist: Google Brain and DeepMind pursue narrower, algorithm-first strategies, while OpenAI's startup-like bet on pure scaling is what actually produced GPT-3, and no rival has yet matched it.

n0103.title: Critiquing The Critics
n0103.gist: The past decade shows that scaling skeptics were repeatedly and confidently wrong while a few scaling believers were vindicated, exposing how little authority equals predictive accuracy.

n0104.title: A Decade Of Progress
n0104.gist: In just ten years deep learning went from a fringe pursuit to models with hundreds of billions of parameters, exactly as Moravec's hardware forecasts predicted.

n0110.title: Just X Dismissals
n0110.gist: Dismissing large models as 'just' simple mechanisms misses that any successful reduction of intelligence must look exactly like a well-defined algorithm, as OpenAI's own engineers found while waiting in vain to hit a wall.

n0116.title: Authority Without Accountability
n0116.gist: Respectable experts confidently forecast AI winters and dismissed scaling for years, were proven wrong, and never corrected themselves, because authoritative tone tracks social status rather than falsifiable claims.

n0122.title: It From Byte
n0122.gist: Because generative models learn by imitating agents in their training data, agency is a continuum that can emerge unpredictably from almost any sufficiently rich modeling task, not a discrete property that can be safely filtered out.

n0123.title: It From Byte
n0123.gist: GPT-3 already behaves as an agent because imitating human-generated text means imitating agents, and this generalizes to real-world action whenever it is given effectors.

n0132.title: All Is Atoms & Void
n0132.gist: Agency has no special physical substrate, since agentic behavior is ultimately built from the same non-agentic physics as everything else.

n0136.title: Intentional Interpretive Stance
n0136.gist: Treating natural systems like rivers or physics itself as goal-seeking agents is a genuinely useful predictive shortcut, one a scaled-up model is equally likely to adopt.

n0145.title: What Induces Agency Emergence
n0145.gist: Agentic, variational shortcuts are only worth learning when a model faces enough varied, rich problems to reward them, as illustrated by whether even simple systems like Conway's Game of Life could induce them.

n0155.title: Turing Machine Agency
n0155.gist: Even training on abstract Turing machines can push a model toward something like inferring intent, since predicting an unknown machine's rules resembles inferring what an agent wants.

n0165.title: Ambient Agency
n0165.gist: Because agency is a convergent, useful capability rather than a discrete tagged property, no amount of careful data curation can guarantee a powerful model stays free of it.
